ideas.sourceBook: Designing Sound
ideas.prompt: Build a phase check where phase cancellation and delay becomes audible in one small decision: set a rule for when the sound appears, disappears, thickens or decays. Keep it testable inside an eight- or sixteen-bar Neon Orbit section. Give the drummer or live arrangement one clear cue for when it should open up.
ideas.neonOrbitUse: Translate Andy Farnell's procedural-audio thinking into a Neon Orbit move: the sound should behave, respond or evolve instead of sitting still.

ideas.sourceBook: Designing Sound
ideas.prompt: Design a transition based on phase cancellation and delay. give the sound an origin, a body and a destination, even if all three are imaginary. The transition should change the physical feel of the track, not merely add an effect. Try it first with a field recording or guitar fragment, then with a synthetic source.
ideas.neonOrbitUse: Make the behaviour controllable with one or two macros so it can become part of a live set rather than a one-off experiment.
